Battle Mechanics Guide

This document describes core mechanics that determine how damage and turn order work in Pokémon battles.

--------------------------------------------------
Same-Type Attack Bonus (STAB)
--------------------------------------------------

- If a Pokémon uses a move that matches its type, the move’s damage is increased
- Standard STAB multiplier: 1.5×
- Some abilities (e.g., Adaptability) increase STAB to 2×

--------------------------------------------------
Critical Hits
--------------------------------------------------

- Critical hits deal increased damage (1.5×)
- Ignore negative stat changes on the attacker
- Ignore positive stat boosts on the defender
- Occur randomly, with increased chance for certain moves and abilities

--------------------------------------------------
Turn Order and Speed
--------------------------------------------------

moves and abilities

--------------------------------------------------
Turn Order and Speed
--------------------------------------------------

- Pokémon act in order of Speed stat (higher Speed moves first)
- Priority moves can override Speed (e.g., Quick Attack)
- Status conditions like Paralysis reduce Speed and affect turn order

--------------------------------------------------
Accuracy and Evasion
--------------------------------------------------

- Moves have an accuracy percentage that determines if they hit
- Accuracy and evasion can be modified by moves and abilities
- Some moves never miss under certain conditions

--------------------------------------------------
Damage Basics
--------------------------------------------------

miss under certain conditions

--------------------------------------------------
Damage Basics
--------------------------------------------------

Damage depends on:
- Attacking stat (Attack or Special Attack)
- Defending stat (Defense or Special Defense)
- Move power
- Type effectiveness
- STAB bonus
- Random variation

--------------------------------------------------
Key Rules
--------------------------------------------------

- Type effectiveness and STAB stack together
- Critical hits are calculated after most modifiers
- Only one Pokémon acts at a time per turn
- Battle outcomes depend on combining multiple mechanics

Berry Guide

Berries are consumable held items that activate automatically under specific conditions in battle. 
They can restore HP, cure status conditions, boost stats, reduce damage, or provide other one-time effects.

Berries were introduced early in the Pokémon series and later became an important part of held item strategy. Many Berries are used in competitive play because they can improve survivability or activate at key moments. 

--------------------------------------------------
Main Types of Berries
--------------------------------------------------

HP Recovery Berries:
- Restore HP when the holder falls below a certain threshold
- Example: Sitrus Berry restores HP when the Pokémon is low on health

Recovery Berries:
- Restore HP when the holder falls below a certain threshold
- Example: Sitrus Berry restores HP when the Pokémon is low on health

Status-Healing Berries:
- Cure a specific status condition automatically
- Examples:
 - Cheri Berry cures paralysis
 - Chesto Berry cures sleep
 - Pecha Berry cures poison
 - Rawst Berry cures burn
 - Aspear Berry cures freeze

PP Recovery Berries:
- Restore PP for a move under certain conditions

Confusion-Healing Berries:
- Cure confusion when triggered

All-Purpose Healing Berries:
- Cure multiple major conditions or provide broader recovery effects

Damage-Reducing Berries:
- Reduce damage from a specific type of attack once
- These are useful for surviving super-effective hits

Stat-Boosting Berries:
- Raise a stat when HP is low
- Examples include Berries that can boost Speed, Attack, or other stats

Berry Mechanics
--------------------------------------------------

- Berries are usually consumed after activation
- A Pokémon can hold only one item at a time
- Berry activation often depends on HP thresholds or battle conditions
- Some abilities and moves can interact with Berries
- Berries are widely used as held items for recovery, utility, and defensive planning

- Status-healing Berries reduce disruption from burn, sleep, poison, and paralysis

Choice Items Guide

Choice Items are held items that boost one stat by 50% but lock the Pokémon into the first move it uses until it switches out.

These items are widely used in competitive play because they provide a strong immediate advantage in power or speed.

--------------------------------------------------
Main Choice Items
--------------------------------------------------

Choice Band:
- Increases Attack by 50%
- Locks the user into the first move selected
- Best used on physical attackers

Choice Specs:
- Increases Special Attack by 50%
- Locks the user into the first move selected
- Best used on special attackers

Choice Scarf:
- Increases Speed by 50%
- Locks the user into the first move selected
- Best used to outspeed opponents

--------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------
Choice Item Mechanics
--------------------------------------------------

- The held Pokémon can only use the first move it selects
- The move lock remains until the Pokémon switches out
- Status moves can also cause the user to become locked
- Switching resets the lock
- Choice Items are not consumed after use

--------------------------------------------------
Competitive Use
--------------------------------------------------

- Choice Band is used to maximize physical damage output
- Choice Specs is used to maximize special damage output
- Choice Scarf is used to gain speed control and revenge kill faster threats
- These items are strong but require prediction because the move lock can be exploited

Defensive Items Guide

Defensive items are held items that reduce damage taken, improve defenses, or increase survivability in battle. 
They are commonly used to make Pokémon harder to defeat or to survive key attacks.

--------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------

- Increases Special Defense by 50%
- Prevents the use of status moves

Eviolite:

- Only works if the Pokémon can still evolve

Rocky Helmet:
- Deals damage to attackers when they make contact (1/6 of their max HP)

Air Balloon:
- Grants immunity to Ground-type moves
- Pops after the Pokémon is hit

Heavy-Duty Boots:
- Prevents damage and effects from entry hazards

Focus Band:

Entry Hazards Guide

Entry hazards are battlefield effects that damage or affect Pokémon when they switch into battle. 
They remain on the field until removed and primarily impact grounded Pokémon.

--------------------------------------------------
Types of Entry Hazards
--------------------------------------------------

Stealth Rock:
- Deals damage based on the Pokémon’s weakness or resistance to Rock-type moves
- Damage ranges from 1/32 (resisted) up to 1/2 (4× weakness) of max HP

Spikes:
- Damages grounded Pokémon when they switch in
- 1 layer: 1/8 of max HP
- 2 layers: 1/6 of max HP
- 3 layers: 1/4 of max HP

Toxic Spikes:
- Poisons grounded Pokémon when they switch in
- 1 layer: regular poison
- 2 layers: badly poisoned (increasing damage each turn)

Sticky Web:
- Lowers Speed of grounded Pokémon upon switch-in

- 2 layers: badly poisoned (increasing damage each turn)

--------------------------------------------------
Hazard Mechanics
--------------------------------------------------

- Only affect Pokémon when they enter the field
- Flying-type Pokémon and those with Levitate are immune to ground-based hazards (Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Sticky Web)
- Stealth Rock affects all Pokémon regardless of grounding
- Multiple hazards can be active at the same time
- Hazards can be removed by moves such as Rapid Spin or Defog

--------------------------------------------------
Competitive Impact
--------------------------------------------------

- Hazards apply constant pressure by dealing damage over time
- They punish frequent switching
- They can break Focus Sash and reduce survivability
- Often used in competitive play to control the pace of battle

--------------------------------------------------
Ability Interaction
--------------------------------------------------

Some abilities interact with entry hazards.

Examples:
- Magic Guard: Prevents damage from hazards
- Levitate: Grants immunity to ground-based hazards
- Overcoat: Prevents damage from certain indirect effects

Pokémon Ability Guide

This document describes Pokémon abilities, which are passive effects that influence battle mechanics. Each Pokémon can have one or more abilities that activate automatically under certain conditions.

Abilities can affect damage, status conditions, weather, switching mechanics, and other battle interactions.

--------------------------------------------------
What is an Ability?
--------------------------------------------------
An ability is a passive trait assigned to a Pokémon that provides special effects in battle or in the overworld. Abilities do not require activation by the player and are always in effect unless suppressed.

Each Pokémon species may have:
- One or two standard abilities
- One hidden ability (rarer, often obtained through special methods)

--------------------------------------------------
Ability Categories
--------------------------------------------------

1. Offensive Abilities
These abilities increase damage output or apply pressure to opponents.

Examples:
- Huge Power: Doubles the Pokémon’s Attack stat
- Blaze: Boosts Fire-type moves when HP is low
- Adaptability: Increases same-type attack bonus (STAB)

--------------------------------------------------

2. Defensive Abilities
These abilities reduce damage taken or provide immunity.

Examples:
- Levitate: Grants immunity to Ground-type moves
- Thick Fat: Reduces damage from Fire and Ice moves
- Sturdy: Prevents being knocked out in one hit from full HP

3. Status-Based Abilities
These abilities interact with status conditions.

Examples:
- Guts: Increases Attack when affected by a status condition
- Immunity: Prevents poisoning
- Synchronize: Passes status conditions to the opponent

--------------------------------------------------

4. Weather-Based Abilities
These abilities activate or benefit from weather conditions.

Examples:
- Drizzle: Summons rain when entering battle
- Drought: Summons harsh sunlight
- Swift Swim: Doubles Speed in rain

Ability Mechanics

- Abilities activate automatically without player input
- Some abilities trigger on entry into battle
- Some abilities activate under specific conditions (e.g., low HP, weather)
- Certain moves and abilities can suppress or ignore abilities

Pokémon Status Conditions Guide

This document describes status conditions, which are effects that impact a Pokémon’s ability to battle. These conditions can reduce stats, prevent actions, or deal damage over time.

Status conditions are divided into two main categories: non-volatile and volatile.

--------------------------------------------------
Types of Status Conditions
--------------------------------------------------

1. Non-Volatile Status Conditions
These are major status conditions that persist even after switching out and often last until healed.

A Pokémon can only have ONE non-volatile status condition at a time.

Examples include:
- Burn
- Paralysis
- Poison
- Sleep
- Freeze

These conditions usually require healing through items, abilities, or visiting a Pokémon Center.

--------------------------------------------------

2.

conditions usually require healing through items, abilities, or visiting a Pokémon Center.

--------------------------------------------------

2. Volatile Status Conditions
These are temporary effects that only last during battle or for a limited number of turns.

A Pokémon can have multiple volatile conditions at the same time.

Examples include:
- Confusion
- Flinch
- Infatuation

These conditions typically wear off after a few turns or when the Pokémon switches out.

--------------------------------------------------
Common Status Conditions
--------------------------------------------------

Burn:
- Deals damage each turn (1/16 of max HP)
- Reduces physical Attack stat by 50%

Paralysis:
- Reduces Speed to 50% of its original value
- 25% chance each turn that the Pokémon cannot move

Poison:
- Deals damage each turn (1/8 of max HP)

Badly Poisoned (Toxic):

Sleep:
- Prevents the Pokémon from acting for 1–3 turns

Freeze:
- Prevents the Pokémon from acting
- Has a chance each turn to thaw (or can be cured by certain moves)

Confusion (volatile):
- Lasts 1–4 turns
- Each turn, there is a chance (~33%) the Pokémon hurts itself instead of attacking

--------------------------------------------------
Battle Impact
--------------------------------------------------

- Status conditions can significantly weaken a Pokémon
- Some abilities and moves rely on status conditions
- Certain types are immune to specific conditions

Healing and Removal

- Moves (e.g., Aromatherapy)
- Abilities (e.g., Natural Cure)
- Visiting a Pokémon Center

--------------------------------------------------
Important Rules
--------------------------------------------------

- Only one non-volatile status condition can be active at a time 
- Multiple volatile conditions can stack 
- Non-volatile conditions persist outside battle until healed

Terrain Effects Guide

Terrain conditions are battlefield effects that influence grounded Pokémon. 
Only Pokémon that are touching the ground are affected by terrain effects.

Terrain typically lasts for several turns and can be set by moves or abilities.

--------------------------------------------------
Types of Terrain
--------------------------------------------------

Electric Terrain:
- Boosts Electric-type move damage by 30%
- Prevents grounded Pokémon from falling asleep
- Activates abilities such as Surge Surfer

Grassy Terrain:
- Restores 1/16 of max HP each turn for grounded Pokémon
- Boosts Grass-type move damage by 30%
- Reduces damage from certain ground-based moves (e.g., Earthquake)

Misty Terrain:
- Reduces Dragon-type move damage by 50% on grounded targets
- Prevents status conditions on grounded Pokémon

- Prevents status conditions on grounded Pokémon

Psychic Terrain:
- Boosts Psychic-type move damage by 30%
- Prevents priority moves from hitting grounded Pokémon

--------------------------------------------------
Terrain Mechanics
--------------------------------------------------

- Terrain effects last 5 turns
- Duration can be extended to 8 turns with held items (e.g., Terrain Extender)
- Only one terrain can be active at a time
- Flying-type Pokémon and those with Levitate are not affected

--------------------------------------------------

Utility and Offensive Items Guide

Utility and offensive items are held items that provide unique effects, boost damage, or trigger under specific conditions. 
These items are commonly used in competitive play to gain strategic advantages.

--------------------------------------------------
Main Utility and Offensive Items
--------------------------------------------------

Life Orb:
- Increases damage by 30%
- User loses 10% of max HP after each damaging attack

Focus Sash:
- If the Pokémon is at full HP, it survives a hit with 1 HP
- Only activates once per battle

Weakness Policy:
- Raises Attack and Special Attack by 2 stages when hit by a super-effective move

Expert Belt:
- Boosts damage of super-effective moves by 20%

Weather Effects Guide

Weather conditions are battlefield effects that influence damage, abilities, and other battle mechanics. Weather typically lasts for several turns and can be extended by certain abilities or items.

--------------------------------------------------
Types of Weather
--------------------------------------------------

Rain:
- Boosts Water-type moves by 50%
- Reduces Fire-type move damage by 50%
- Activates certain abilities (e.g., Swift Swim, Rain Dish)

Sun (Harsh Sunlight):
- Boosts Fire-type moves by 50%
- Reduces Water-type move damage by 50%
- Activates certain abilities (e.g., Chlorophyll, Solar Power)

Sandstorm:
- Damages most Pokémon each turn (1/16 of max HP)
- Does not damage Rock, Ground, or Steel types
- Boosts Special Defense of Rock-type Pokémon by 50%
- Activates abilities such as Sand Rush and Sand Force
